sections.reason: Title block, Status of this Memo, copyright notice, Abstract and table of contents. The Abstract states what the memo adds to RADIUS and binds no speaker.
Introduction. Says what RFC 2865 and RFC 2866 describe, that the new attributes are experimental, and that attributes are Type-Length-Value triples. No obligation.

Specification of Requirements. The RFC 2119 key-words paragraph, the compliant / unconditionally compliant / conditionally compliant definitions, and one normative paragraph that scopes the document's other requirements to the services a NAS offers. The three sites below come from that last paragraph.

Terminology. Defines service, session and 'silently discard'. The 'silently discard' entry carries two SHOULD clauses about logging the error and counting the event; neither is gated and neither is declared in rfc/short/rfc2869.md.
Operation. One sentence: operation is identical to RFC 2865 and RFC 2866. No obligation of its own.
RADIUS support for Interim Accounting Updates. Two capitalised MUSTs, both binding the NAS, both classified below.

RADIUS support for Apple Remote Access Protocol. Describes ARAP's two-way DES exchange and the ARAP attribute set. Ze implements no ARAP: internal/component/radius/dict.go declares no attribute in the 70-74 or 84 range, and internal/component/l2tp/ppp offers PAP, CHAP and MS-CHAPv2 only.
RADIUS Support for Extensible Authentication Protocol. Introduces EAP-Message and Message-Authenticator. No capitalised keyword.

Protocol Overview. Twelve capitalised MUSTs describing an EAP conversation carried over RADIUS. Ze carries no EAP over RADIUS: internal/component/radius/dict.go declares no EAP-Message attribute (type 79), and internal/component/l2tp/ppp has no EAP module, so LCP never negotiates EAP. Ze's IKEv2 EAP (internal/core/eap) terminates EAP locally and imports no RADIUS package.

Retransmission. Says the NAS retransmits between peer and NAS and the RADIUS client retransmits between client and server, and that Session-Timeout in an Access-Challenge bounds the wait for an EAP-Response. Indicative prose, no capitalised keyword.
Fragmentation. Says Framed-MTU may be included in an Access-Request carrying an EAP-Message. Permissive, no capitalised keyword.
Examples. Two message-sequence diagrams of an OTP authentication. Illustration only.
Alternative uses. One capitalised MUST binding a RADIUS server that proxies RADIUS-encapsulated EAP to a backend security server.
Packet Format. One sentence: identical to RFC 2865 and RFC 2866.
Packet Types. Identical to RFC 2865 and RFC 2866, and points at the Table of Attributes.

Attributes. The attribute type list and the five data types. The section states that 'A summary of the attribute format is the same as in RFC 2865 [1] but is included here for ease of reference', so its three capitalised MUSTs restate RFC 2865 Section 5.

Acct-Input-Gigawords. Defines type 52 and says the attribute 'indicates how many times the Acct-Input-Octets counter has wrapped around 2^32 over the course of this service being provided, and can only be present in Accounting-Request records where the Acct-Status-Type is set to Stop or Interim-Update'. Indicative prose with no capitalised keyword, which is why the site scan sees nothing here. The five gated Gigawords rows in rfc/short/rfc2869.md were all read from this sentence and its identically worded twin in Section 5.2, so they are declared unsourced here.

Acct-Output-Gigawords. Defines type 53 in wording identical to Section 5.1 with Acct-Output-Octets substituted. The five gated rows it shares with Section 5.1 are declared unsourced on Section 5.1 rather than twice.
Event-Timestamp. Defines type 55 as the time the event occurred. No obligation.
ARAP-Password. Defines type 70. Ze implements no ARAP.
ARAP-Features. Defines type 71. Ze implements no ARAP.
ARAP-Zone-Access. Defines type 72. Ze implements no ARAP.
ARAP-Security. Defines type 73. Ze implements no ARAP.
ARAP-Security-Data. Defines type 74. Ze implements no ARAP.
Password-Retry. Defines type 75, how many attempts a user is allowed. Ze declares no such attribute constant.
Prompt. Defines type 76, whether the NAS echoes the user's response. Ze declares no such attribute constant.
Connect-Info. Defines type 77, the connect speed the NAS reports. Ze declares no such attribute constant.
Configuration-Token. Defines type 78, for a RADIUS proxy. Ze is no RADIUS proxy.
EAP-Message. Defines type 79 and six capitalised MUSTs over its handling. Ze declares no EAP-Message attribute constant and sends and receives none.

Message-Authenticator. Defines type 80, its two HMAC-MD5 formulas, and three capitalised MUSTs. The third binds a RADIUS client, which is the role Ze plays (internal/component/radius/client.go), and is captured as RFC2869-5.14-1.
ARAP-Challenge-Response. Defines type 84. Ze implements no ARAP.

Acct-Interim-Interval. Defines type 85 and one capitalised MUST NOT over the value the sender puts in it. The section states the attribute 'can only appear in the Access-Accept message', so the obligation binds the RADIUS server.

NAS-Port-Id. Defines type 87 as UTF-8 text of length 3 or more naming the physical port. Its one obligation is a SHOULD read from indicative prose, which the site scan does not surface and which rfc/short/rfc2869.md declares as RFC2869-5.17-1.
Framed-Pool. Defines type 88, the address pool name. No obligation.
Table of Attributes heading and its opening paragraph. The table body, Note 1 and the notation legend fall outside the numbered-section split and are carried by the derived section '0'.

The tail of Section 5.19: the packet-versus-attribute table, Note 1, and the legend defining 0, 0+, 0-1 and 1. The section splitter cannot attribute this block to a numbered heading, so it derives as section '0'.
IANA Considerations. Registers the packet type codes, attribute types and attribute values from the RADIUS name spaces per BCP 26. Binds IANA, not a speaker.
Security Considerations. One sentence: the attributes other than Message-Authenticator and EAP-Message add nothing beyond RFC 2865.
Message-Authenticator Security. Explains why an Access-Request without a User-Password should carry a Message-Authenticator. Lowercase 'should', no capitalised keyword.
EAP Security. Lists the five threats the subsections address. No obligation.
Separation of EAP server and PPP authenticator. Describes key transport between the EAP server and the PPP authenticator. No capitalised keyword.
Connection hijacking. One capitalised MUST requiring every EAP/RADIUS packet to be authenticated with the Message-Authenticator attribute.
Man in the middle attacks. States that a compromised RADIUS proxy can modify EAP packets. No countermeasure is directed at a speaker.
Multiple databases. Recommends consolidating the RADIUS and backend security databases. Advice to a deployer, no capitalised keyword.
Negotiation attacks. Eight capitalised keywords across the authenticating peer, an EAP-capable NAS, and the RADIUS server or proxy.
References: RFC 2865, RFC 2866, RFC 2284, RFC 2119, RFC 1700, RFC 2868, RFC 2867, RFC 2279, RFC 2104, RFC 2434 and one informative citation.
Acknowledgements.
Chair's Address. A postal and mail address block, matching how rfc/extraction/rfc3765.json skips its Author's Address section.
Authors' Addresses. Address blocks only.
Full Copyright Statement. The ISOC boilerplate and its disclaimer.

sites.quote: A NAS that does not implement a given service MUST NOT implement the RADIUS attributes for that service.
sites.reason: Binds the NAS, which is the role Ze plays (internal/component/l2tp is the LNS and NAS side). Captured as RFC2869-1.1-1 at [MUST NOT]. Ze's NAS offers PPP with PAP, CHAP-MD5 or MS-CHAPv2 and nothing else, and internal/component/radius/dict.go declares no attribute in the 70-74 or 84 ARAP range and none for EAP-Message (type 79).

sites.quote: For example, a NAS that is unable to offer ARAP service MUST NOT implement the RADIUS attributes for ARAP.
sites.reason: The sentence opens 'For example' and names ARAP as an instance of the rule site 1.1:1 states. It adds no obligation site 1.1:1 does not already carry.

sites.quote: A NAS MUST treat a RADIUS access-request requesting an unavailable service as an access-reject instead.
sites.reason: Binds the NAS. Captured as RFC2869-1.1-2 at [MUST]. buildAuthAttrs (internal/component/l2tp/plugins/authradius/handler.go) names Service-Type Framed and Framed-Protocol PPP in every Access-Request it builds, for every authentication method, so the NAS never requests a service it cannot then provide.

sites.quote: Note that a locally configured value on the NAS MUST override the value found in an Access-Accept.
sites.reason: Binds the NAS, which is the role ze plays. Captured as RFC2869-2.1-2 at [MUST]. acctInterval (internal/component/l2tp/plugins/authradius/acct.go) answers the acct-interval config leaf whenever the operator set one and reads the Access-Accept's Acct-Interim-Interval only when the leaf is absent; the leaf carries no YANG default (yang/ze-l2tp-auth-radius-conf.yang) so the absent case stays representable. The site was left unclassified on the first walk because ze then took the Access-Accept value over the configured one, which is the reverse of this sentence.

sites.quote: Since all the information is cumulative, a NAS MUST ensure that only a single generation of an interim Accounting message for a given session is present in the retransmission queue at any given time.
sites.reason: Binds the NAS. Captured as RFC2869-2.1-1 at [MUST]. interimLoop (internal/component/l2tp/plugins/authradius/acct.go) calls sendAcctInterimUpdate inline on each tick, so a tick that arrives while the previous generation is still retransmitting starts no second generation.

sites.quote: If the user's password is greater than 8 octets in length, an Access-Reject MUST be sent instead.
sites.reason: Binds the RADIUS server. The sentence sits inside the list of attributes the server returns in an ARAP Access-Accept, and the actor is the party that computes ARAP-Challenge-Response by DES-encrypting the dial-in client's challenge with the user's password. Ze is a RADIUS client only (internal/component/radius/client.go opens a UDP socket to send requests and match replies) and implements no ARAP.
